preconditions.description: The length of string P is between 1 and 10^6 inclusive.
The number of queries Q is between 1 and 10^6 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(c in 'chef' for c in P)
preconditions.description: String P consists only of the characters 'c', 'h', 'e', and 'f'.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= L <= R <= len(P) for L, R in queries)
preconditions.description: For every query, the range [L, R] is valid within the 1-based indices of P.

preconditions.expression: all(a != b and a in 'chef' and b in 'chef' for a, b, _, _ in queries)
preconditions.description: For every query, the start character 'a' and end character 'b' are distinct and belong to the set {'c', 'h', 'e', 'f'}.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly Q lines, one for each query.

postconditions.expression: all(int(line) == sum(1 for i in range(L-1, R) for j in range(i+1, R) if P[i] == a and P[j] == b) for line, (a, b, L, R) in zip(stdout_lines, queries))
postconditions.description: For each query (a, b, L, R), the output line is the count of pairs of indices (i, j) such that L-1 <= i < j <= R-1 (0-based), P[i] == a, P[j] == b, and i != j (implied by i < j).
